claims.claim: Lincoln Michel asserts that AI does not have intention and produces automatically, so a generated metaphor is not chosen to emphasise a theme or deepen a character.
claims.modelEra: September 2024, ChatGPT-era, no specific model named; register measured: fiction

claims.claim: Michel asserts that a description of a setting is not merely something to get through but a place to reinforce themes, add atmosphere and deepen character.
claims.quote: a place to reenforce themes, add atmosphere, deepen character
claims.page: section discussing the Verge self-publishing article
claims.polarity: asserts (a human craft standard against which generated setting description is judged)
claims.modelEra: September 2024; human craft standard, no model; register measured: fiction

claims.feature: other: surface polish with nothing underneath
claims.claim: Michel characterises AI-generated work as art that has nothing to say.
claims.quote: art that has nothing to say
claims.modelEra: September 2024, ChatGPT era; register measured: fiction and visual art

claims.feature: other: revision is where quality is made
claims.claim: Michel asserts that the hardest and most time-consuming part of writing is shaping, honing and refining the material, not producing a draft.
claims.quote: The hardest and most time-consuming part of writing is shaping, honing, and refining
claims.modelEra: September 2024; human craft standard; register measured: fiction

claims.claim: Michel contrasts individual human sentences with what he calls the generic averaging of terabytes of training data.
claims.quote: the generic averaging of terabytes of training data
claims.modelEra: September 2025, post-GPT-5 release; register measured: literary fiction

claims.feature: other: visible prose as the human marker
claims.claim: Michel proposes that criticism should celebrate very visible prose, sentences that writhe and shine and sing with the individual behind them.
claims.quote: sentences that writhe and shine and sing with the individual behind them

claims.claim: Michel characterises LLM output as probable-sounding but not necessarily accurate or even coherent.
claims.quote: probable-sounding but not necessarily accurate or even coherent
claims.page: opening section, after the two numbered assumptions
claims.modelEra: September 2025, after GPT-5's release; register measured: general text

claims.claim: Michel states that the danger of LLMs for literature remains their quantity rather than their quality, and that he has never worried much about LLMs replacing authors on quality.
claims.quote: the danger of LLMs for literature remains their quantity, not their quality
claims.page: section 'The Slop Tsunami Could Still Drown Us Though'
claims.polarity: disputes (declines the claim that AI quality is the threat)
claims.modelEra: February 2026; models unnamed; register measured: commercial and literary fiction

claims.claim: Harvey Randall argues that background chatter, combat barks, NPC dialogue and side-quests all matter and are the backbone on which a game's story lies.
claims.source: Harvey Randall, staff writer, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.quote: Background chatter, combat barks, NPC dialogue, side-quests, it all matters.
claims.modelEra: August 2026, on AI-NPC products from Convai, Ubisoft and Meaning Machine; register measured: game dialogue

claims.claim: Randall asserts that hand-written incidental lines such as combat barks characterise an enemy faction and journal entries flesh out a culture.
claims.source: Harvey Randall, staff writer, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.quote: Combat barks can characterise an enemy faction, journal entries can flesh out a culture

claims.claim: Randall argues that Starfield's procedurally generated planets and cities feel bland with all the rough edges sanded off next to New Vegas's hand-crafted background babble.
claims.source: Harvey Randall, staff writer, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.quote: all the rough edges sanded off
claims.modelEra: August 2026; the comparison is procedural generation, not an LLM; register measured: game world text

claims.feature: other: incidental detail builds scale and place
claims.claim: Randall asserts that a game's hundreds of small background lines can create a sense of scale or place rather than only conveying plot information.
claims.source: Harvey Randall, staff writer, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.quote: they can create a sense of scale or place

claims.claim: Adam Smith, Larian's writing director, said in a Reddit AMA that no text generation touches the dialogues, journal entries or other writing in Divinity.
claims.source: Adam Smith (Larian writing director) quoted by Ted Litchfield, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.quote: We don't have any text generation touching our dialogues, journal entries
claims.modelEra: January 2026; models unnamed; register measured: game dialogue and journal entries

claims.claim: Smith reported that Larian's experiments with text-generation tools produced results that hit a 3/10 at best, while his own worst first drafts are at least a 4/10.
claims.source: Adam Smith (Larian writing director) quoted by Ted Litchfield, PC Gamer, 2026
claims.quote: the results hit a 3/10 at best
claims.confidence: high — note the PC Gamer headline says 4/10 as '3/10 worse than his worst drafts'; the AMA text itself gives 3/10 versus at least 4/10
claims.modelEra: January 2026; tools unnamed; register measured: game dialogue
